# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (use instead of source text)

Two separate books, under headings BOOK 1 and BOOK 2.

---

## BOOK 1 of 2: STRONG POISON (Dorothy L. Sayers, 1930; Gutenberg 78157)

**Epigraph:** Old ballad "Lord Rendal": "Where gat ye your dinner, Lord Rendal, my son?"... "O that was strong poison, Lord Rendal..."

**Characters**
- **Harriet Vane**: prisoner, mystery novelist, age 29, dark smudged eyes, square brows. Accused of murdering Philip Boyes with arsenic. Lived with Boyes ~1 year (from March 1928) without marriage; quarreled Feb 1929 when Boyes offered marriage (she felt it was "a bad-conduct prize"/a test). Moved to Doughty Street flat, No. 100.
- **Philip Boyes**: deceased, 36, writer (5 novels, essays), "advanced" views (atheism, free love). Cousin of Norman Urquhart; son of Rev. Arthur Boyes (Tweedling Parva vicarage). Had recurring gastric attacks (Mar 31, Apr 15, May 12, 1929). Died 23 June 1929, 3 a.m.
- **Lord Peter Wimsey**: amateur detective, ~40, fair hair, monocle, valet **Bunter**. Mother: Dowager Duchess of Denver. Brother: Gerald, Duke of Denver; Duchess Helen. Sister: Lady Mary. Car "Mrs. Merdle." Friend Hon. **Freddy Arbuthnot**. Chief-Inspector **Charles Parker** (Scotland Yard). Lodges Piccadilly (110a).
- **Sir Impey Biggs**: defence counsel. **Mr. Crofts** of Crofts & Cooper, solicitors. **Attorney-General** (prosecutor). Judge: old, parrot-faced (first trial), later plump, eighteenth-century-faced.
- **Norman Urquhart**: cousin, solicitor, Woburn Square house, office Bedford Row. Pale, freckled, dark sleek hair, 40s.
- **Hannah Westlock**: parlourmaid. **Mrs. Pettican**: cook.
- **Dr. Grainger**, **Dr. Weare**: physicians. **Nurse Williams**: talked of arsenic.
- **Ryland Vaughan**: friend, tall, mournful; carries vial. Inherited copyrights.
- **Sylvia Marriott** (sprained ankle, Doughty St-area), **Eiluned Price** (stout, pugnacious), **Joey Trimbles**.
- **Marjorie Phelps**: porcelain figurine maker, Wimsey's friend.
- **Miss Katharine Climpson**: elderly spinster juror, runs "The Cattery" typing bureau; holds out for acquittal.
- **Mr. Challoner**: Vane's literary agent. **Mr. Trufoot**: publisher. **Mr. Cole** (Grimsby & Cole, publishers of Boyes).
- **Mrs. Bulfinch** (née Montague, "Gracie"), ex-barmaid at the Nine Rings, Gray's Inn Road.
- **Mrs. Wrayburn** (stage name Cremorna Garden / Rosanna), actress, great-aunt, Windle, Westmorland, paralysed; will leaves real estate + £50,000 to Philip Boyes, residue to Norman.
- **Miss Murchison (Joan)**: typist at Urquhart's office, Wimsey's agent.
- **Miss Booth (Caroline)**: nurse at Appleford, Windle; "Mrs. Craig" medium; "Pongo" control.
- **Bill Rumm ("Blindfold Bill")**: reformed burglar/locksmith; wife Bella; daughter Esmeralda Hyacinth.
- **Mrs. Pegler, Miss Tweall, Miss Etheredge, Mrs. Liffey**: boarding-house ladies, Windle.
- **Mike/Bunter**: Bunter courts Hannah and Mrs. Pettican.

**Key chronology**
- Apr 10 1929: Vane buys 2 oz arsenic (Mr. Brown, Southampton Row), signs "Mary Slater." May 5: weed-killer, "Edith Waters." Also prussic acid, strychnine, aconitine attempt.
- June 16: Boyes letter "Dear Harriet... cut adrift and take a trip out West"; reply "You can come round at 9.30 on the 20th... you certainly will not make me change my mind," signed "M."
- June 20: dinner at Urquhart's (sherry 1847 Oloroso, cold bouillon, turbot, poulet en casserole, sweet omelette made by Boyes with 4 eggs—one cracked—and jam; Burgundy Corton drunk by Boyes alone, sealed). Boyes leaves 9:15, arrives Doughty St 9:25; leaves ~10; taxi from Guilford St 10:10; collapses at Woburn Sq.
- Bulfinch testimony (Ch. X): ~10:05 Boyes at Nine Rings, double Martell; left white paper packet with powder in it; packet hidden behind bar, later found and proved to be bicarbonate of soda.
- Boyes died 23 June 3 a.m.; funeral 28th. Exhumation; ~4–5 grains arsenic.
- Hair analysis: arsenic near roots ~10 weeks before.

**Trial outcome**: First trial jury deadlocks (Climpson holds out). Retrial; Crown withdraws charge; verdict Not Guilty. Wimsey proposes; Harriet hesitant. Final line: Wimsey: "If she'll have me."

**Solution (Wimsey, Ch. XX–XXII)**: Urquhart secretly immunised himself with arsenic (ss "Styrian" method), poisoned the cracked egg in omelette, shared it with Boyes. Arsenic found in Urquhart's cupboard/panel (Parker/Murchison found packet; Marsh test). Urquhart confronted, collapses; in Ch. XXII he eats Turkish delight with arsenic; arrested.

**Notable quotes**: "Charles, acushla..."; "Strong poison" (ballad title).

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: LINDA CARLTON'S PERILOUS SUMMER (Edith Lavell, A.L. Burt, 1932; Gutenberg 63407)

**Characters**
- **Linda Carlton**: 18, aviatrix, flies autogiro "Ladybug"; first girl to fly NY–Paris alone; lives Green Falls, Michigan, with **Aunt Emily Carlton** (fears planes).
- **Dot (Dorothy) Crowley**: chum, diminutive; boyfriend **Jim Valier**.
- **Amy** (rescued girl; real name **Helen Tower**, 14): named after Amy Johnson; amnesia, fears ghosts/dark/water.
- **Ralph Clavering**: wealthy suitor; autogiro; sister **Kit (Kitty) Hulbert**, husband **Tom Hulbert** (Lt., U.S. Flying Corps); father **Mr. Clavering** (R. W.).
- **Harriman (Harry) Smith**: old friend, goes back to work.
- **Lord Dudley (Claude Dudley)**: English "lord," fake—actually **Ed (Edward) Tower**, Helen's uncle. Proposed to Linda.
- **Mike O'Malley**: reporter, Grand Rapids *Star*, freckled, from farm; brother **Pat** (telephone company, truck with ladder).
- **Mrs. Elsie Fishberry** (later "Mrs. Edward Tower" claim): fake aunt, Montana; later repentant.
- **Mrs. Smalley ("Nana")**: Helen's old nurse, deaf, elderly.
- **Leo Epstein**: lawyer who sent threatening telegram ($50,000 suit).
- **Mr. Hudson**: Vice-president, Chicago Trust Company.
- **John Kuhns**: friend of Tom Hulbert.
- **Sue Emery, Sarah Wheeler, Madge & Bert Keen, Joe Elliston, Frank Lawlor, Babs Macy**: friends.
- **Anna**: cook.

**Events**
1. Ch I: Linda & Dot in autogiro; see gray-bearded man in car at 80 mph strike girl on Wisconsin road; land, pick up girl (no memory, fears "ghost"). Taken to Milwaukee hospital; Linda & Dot sensed newspaper publicity.
2. Ch II–IV: Girl named "Amy"; taken to Green Falls. Treasure hunt announced (by airplanes, Lake Winnebago prize). Lord Dudley appears at tennis matches.
3. Ch V–VI: Lord Dudley flights; proposes; Linda refuses elopement. Linda gets telegram from Dudley.
4. Ch VII–VIII: Ralph's autogiro arrives; Mrs. Fishberry claims Amy; Mike blocks; Fishberry/Ed Tower plan to set house afire and sue Linda ($50,000).
5. Ch IX–X: Treasure hunt; storm; Linda finds treasure: check for $1,000 signed R. W. Clavering; $500 for Amy. Linda & Amy at Fox River house; ghost in tower (skeleton with wax face, string-pulled hands). Fishberry takes Amy.
6. Ch XI–XIII: Linda & Dot investigate; Telegram from Epstein. Fishberry leaves Helen locked in house Sat. Helen finds Mrs. Smalley photo, Bible; Nana had been located.
7. Ch XIV–XVII: Lord Dudley claims to be a rescuer; Linda at house; Ed Tower sets fire; Mike and Pat arrive with ladder; girls rescued from tower. Found gray wig and beard (Ed's disguise).
8. Ch XVIII–XIX: Will found hidden in tower; grandfather Henry Adolph Tower's will leaves house and $100,000 to Helen, $5,000 to Mrs. Smalley. Trust Company already paid Ed. Fishberry confesses Ed's plan; Ed fled to air transport from Newport News, Virginia, to England.
9. Ch XX–XXI: Linda & Helen fly over Allegheny Mountains; crash; repair; reach Newport News; find transport ship; Linda lands on deck; "Lord Dudley" revealed as Ed Tower; money (bonds $50,000 + $50,000 cash) recovered. Final: return to Green Falls Monday; Helen reunited with Mrs. Smalley.
